en: The Buddha-spoken *Sūtra of All Buddhas*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Grand Master of the Dharma Transmission and Acting Minister of State for the Court of Ceremonial,
under imperial decree during the Western Heavens Translation Era.
Thus have I heard:

At one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain near the city of Rājagṛha. Then the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana, as the time for his meal approached, put on his robes, took up his bowl, and set out for the royal city. Suddenly, he had this thought:
"On this day, I shall first go to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven to inquire about a certain matter, and then return to beg for alms."
Thereupon, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana entered a state of meditative equipoise (*samādhi*) and, in the time it takes a strong man to bend or extend his arm, arrived at the Akaniṣṭha Heaven.
Having arrived there, he met with the deva and exchanged various gentle words of greeting.
Then, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana asked the deva:
"After how much time will a Buddha, a World-Honored One, appear in the world and realize unsurpassed bodhi?"
Then, the hundred-colored ultimate lords of the heavens replied with one voice:
“After a full hundred thousand kalpas, a Buddha shall appear in the world and realize unexcelled bodhi.”

At that time, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana, having heard this, accepted it with faith; he immediately entered samādhi and, in the time it takes a strong man to bend or extend his arm, returned from Akaniṣṭha Heaven to the royal city, whereupon he went on his almsround as usual, proceeding in due order.
Having finished eating, washed his hands and mouth, and put away his robes and bowl, he went to where the Buddha was.
He prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet; having completed his respectful salutation, he sat to one side, joined his palms in reverence, gazed up at the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One, today as the time for my meal approached, I entered samādhi and went to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven to question the devas there.”
"At what time will a Buddha appear in the world and realize unsurpassed bodhi?
Those lords of a hundred heavens replied to me with one voice:
"After a full hundred thousand kalpas, a Buddha will appear in the world and realize unsurpassed bodhi."
“World-Honored One!
Although I have faith and acceptance, what is the meaning of this matter?
I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain it for me.”
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Mahāmaudgalyāyana:
"Listen attentively now; I shall speak for you. Mahāmaudgalyāyana!"
That Lord of Akaniṣṭha, possessing very little knowledge and vision, said to you:
"Only once in a full hundred thousand kalpas does a Buddha appear in the world to realize unsurpassed bodhi."
"This is not the correct statement; it is not yet to be deeply trusted. Mahāmaudgalyāyana!

I recall that in the past, I first encountered sixty koṭis of Tathāgatas appearing in the world. Those Buddhas remained in the world to benefit sentient beings for either long or short periods, each entering parinirvāṇa in succession according to their conditions."
In this manner, one after another, there appeared eighty koṭis of Buddhas in the world, all named Subhūṣita (Wondrous Flower).
Before each of these Buddhas, I made great vows and maintained the pure conduct of a brahmacārin.
After this Buddha, there appeared in the world another five hundred Buddhas, all named Samyakbrahma.
After these Buddhas, there appeared in the world another eight hundred Buddhas, all named Dīpaṃkara.
After this Buddha, there appeared another fifteen thousand Buddhas, all bearing the same name, Jñānamati.
Following these Buddhas, another thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, each with a different name and lineage.
In the presence of such a Buddha, I further made a vow to practice the holy life (*brahmacarya*).
After this Buddha, there appeared in the world six thousand other Buddhas, all named Subhadrāpa.
After this Buddha, ninety thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, all bearing the same name, Sunetra-Kāśyapa.
After these Buddhas, another thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, all bearing the same name, Sūrya.
After this Buddha, there appeared in the world another thousand Buddhas, all named Raṇajaha.
After these Buddhas, there appeared in the world another eighty thousand Buddhas, all named Airāvaṇa.
After this Buddha, seventy thousand other Buddhas appeared in the world, all bearing the same name, Śakra.
Following these Buddhas, there was yet another Buddha who appeared in the world, named Guṇa.
I, together with the śrāvaka disciples, made a vow before this Buddha to reverently make offerings to him.
After many years had passed, following this Buddha, eighty koṭis of nayutas of pratyekabuddhas appeared in the world.

"Mahāmaudgalyāyana! That Pratyekabuddha made a great vow before me; likewise, there was a Wheel-Turning King named Samantaprabhāsa who, also before me, first encountered forty Buddhas of the same name, Anabhibhū."
Mahāmaudgalyāyana! After the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha Guṇa, I encountered another Buddha also named Anabhibhū.
During the lifetime of this Buddha, I was a wheel-turning sage king named Śata-nāman; together with the śrāvaka disciples of Buddha Anabhibhū, I made a solemn vow and reverently made offerings.
After many years had passed following the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, I constructed a stūpa with the seven precious gems and made offerings to his relics.
I practiced in this manner for immeasurable time.
"Mahāmaudgalyāyana! At that time, I attained the realization of Bodhi.
Furthermore, Mahāmaudgalyāyana!"
Those in the Akaniṣṭha Heaven have but little knowledge and little vision.
After the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha Anabhibhū, another Buddha appeared in the world, named Lokadhara.
Later, there appeared another Buddha in the world named Dharanidhara.
Later, there appeared another Buddha in the world named Mahāśākya-muni.
Later, there appeared another Buddha in the world named Suvyūha.
After that, there was another Buddha named Siṃha who appeared in the world.
After that, there was another Buddha named Paramāścarya who appeared in the world.
Afterward, there was another Buddha named Cuts Off All Sorrow who appeared in the world.
Afterward, there was yet another Buddha named Accomplishment of All Meanings who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Jitāvin who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Ratnaprabha who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Icchānta who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Upatiṣya who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Tiśru who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Parimaṇḍalābha who appeared in the world.
After that, there was another Buddha named Moonlight who appeared in the world.
After that, there was another Buddha named Heavenly Light who appeared in the world.
Later, there was another Buddha named Aditya who appeared in the world.
Later, there was yet another Buddha named Adityajyotis who appeared in the world.
Later, there was another Buddha named Unobstructed Penetration who appeared in the world.
Later, there was yet another Buddha named Most Victorious who appeared in the world.
After that, there was another Buddha named Tiśyadarśana who appeared in the world.
After that, there was another Buddha named Utpalavarna who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Ariṣṭa who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Atibhu who appeared in the world.
Later, there was another Buddha named Dīpaṃkara who appeared in the world.
Later, there was yet another Buddha named Arindama who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Suvarṇaprabha who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Suvarṇābha who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Ratnanetra who appeared in the world.
Afterwards, there was another Buddha named Padmanetra who appeared in the world.
Later, there was another Buddha named Uttamalocana who appeared in the world.
Later, there was yet another Buddha named Mahāpadma who appeared in the world.
Later, there was another Buddha named Padma who appeared in the world.
Later still, there was another Buddha named Vipaśyin who appeared in the world.
After him, there was another Buddha named Śikhin who appeared in the world.
After him, there was another Buddha named Viśvabhū who appeared in the world.
After that, there was another Buddha named Krakucchanda who appeared in the world.
After that, there was another Buddha named Kanakamuni who appeared in the world.
Later, there was another Buddha named Kāśyapa who appeared in the world.
Now, I, Śākyamuni, have appeared in the world. Mahāmaudgalyāyana!
I previously made this vow: "Only after I have scattered offerings of seven-jeweled flowers upon such Buddhas as these shall I attain manifestly perfect enlightenment."
“Mahāmaudgalyāyana! Each and every one of those Buddhas, from their first aspiration until their attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment, all underwent incalculable kalpas.”
From the time I first resolved to attain enlightenment until my achievement of Buddhahood, the number of kalpas has been exceedingly vast and beyond calculation.
Those in the Akaniṣṭha Heaven know and see but little;
do not harbor doubts.

At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sutra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana’s doubts were immediately dispelled; filled with joy and exultation, he prostrated before the Buddha and withdrew.
